- Model consistently overestimates prices in early forecast windows, especially after sharp spikes; reduce initial forecast values by 2–5% for 1–3 day horizons.
- After a price spike, model tends to overshoot and fail to correct downward; apply a “cool-down” penalty: subtract 0.5–1.5% per day after peak until price stabilizes.
- When sentiment is neutral or flat (all 0.00), model exhibits high variance and overconfidence; cap forecast range within ±1.5% of recent 7-day moving average.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon; if forecast is >1.5% above recent 30-day average, reduce by 0.5–1.0% per day until convergence.
- If true outcome shows sharp downward trend after a spike, model often fails to recognize it; add a “reversal buffer” — if 3 consecutive days show >1.5% drop, reduce forecast by 1–2% for next 3 days.
- For 30-day forecasts, model underestimates volatility in low-price regimes; increase forecast variance by 0.5–1.0% when price <35.00 to account for sudden drops.
